newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 12.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Staples and Office Depot continued their negotiations about possibly selling some office supply stores in an effort to head off a federal antitrust challenge to their $4 billion combination.
* Fourth quarter productivity grew more slowly and labor costs grew faster than expected.
* AMR's American Airlines and its pilots are scheduled to resume labor negotiations tomorrow.
* Niagara Mohawk's $4 billion plan to end or restructure its above-market power purchase pacts is a small step toward dealing with $46 billion in such pacts in the utility industry.
* Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette President Joe Roby earned more than $33 million plus stock options in 1996, what appears to be the biggest total compensation on Wall Street last year.
* Insiders could initiate a surge of stock sales after a Securities and Exchange Commission rule change allowing earlier sales of restricted stock goes into effect April 29.
* K-III Communications presented a plan to cut debt by issuing new stock and selling businesses, including New Woman magazine.
* The Dow industrials rose 5.77 to a record 7,085.16. Bond prices fell and the dollar rose.
* The Chicago Board Options Exchange may cut its index-options contract by half, allowing retail investors smaller pieces of the contract to trade, in an effort to attract more retail businesses.
* Fidelity Magellan has sold much of the bond position it had under former manager Jeffrey Vinik, but some analysts think the fund is unlikely to regain its former glory.

* The developer of Playa Vista, a Los Angeles development that is to become the site of a high-tech facility for DreamWorks SKG, is hoping his project can get back on track after a group of banks led by Chase Manhattan began foreclosure proceedings.

* Credit Suisse First Boston can use an inquiry from the Securities and Exchange Commission which found no problems before the collapse of Orange County's investment pool to defend itself against securities fraud charges.
* Ford will cut the number of vehicles it makes in the second quarter by 1.6 percent, but increase its production of light trucks.

* Bondholders cheered on Friday when Ronald Perelman turned the reins over to Carl Icahn in his fight for control over Marvel Entertainment Group. That's because the Perelman-Icahn pact means the bondholders stand a chance of keeping their equity stake in the beleaguered marketer of comic books and trading cards.

But it turns out that Marvel's banks, led by Chase Manhattan Bank, aren't quite as happy with the plan, say people close to the transaction, becuase they lose an important source of repayment on their $630 million in Marvel bank debt. -- Heard on the Street.

* Treasury prices fell yesterday in volatile trading as investors struggled to digest various economic data and market rumors in their attempt to assess the chances of an interest-rate increase later this month. -- Credit Markets.
